previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence presented with abdominal bloating/distention and increased, discolored G-tube output while taking metronidazole and norfloxacin at home for suspected recurrent small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. She was admitted to the bariatric surgery service and initially managed with bowel rest (NPO), IV fluids, and IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Abdominal radiography showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern without free air, and a contrast G-tube study confirmed a patent tube positioned in the stomach without extraluminal leak. She received soap-suds enemas for distention and was transitioned to IV ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, with restart of tube feeds and advancement to a bariatric Stage V diet, both tolerated without nausea or discomfort. She remained afebrile and clinically improved; blood cultures showed no growth, and stool testing was negative for toxigenic C. difficile and common bacterial pathogens. She was discharged home ambulatory and mentally clear with instructions to continue metronidazole, avoid NSAIDs, remain on Stage V diet, and coordinate tube feed regimen with her bariatric clinic.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History: ___ s/p RNY with G-tube p/w 4d h/o of abd pain  // eval
for constipation, distention

TECHNIQUE:  Upright and supine radiographs of the abdomen.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior radiographs the abdomen dated ___
through ___, and CT of the abdomen and pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Normal bowel gas pattern without evidence of ileus or obstruction.  Moderate
fecal loading in the ascending colon. No pneumatosis or free air. The G-tube
projects over the left hemiabdomen. Surgical clip present in the left upper
quadrant. Visualized osseous structures are unremarkable. Phleboliths project
over the pelvis.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Normal bowel gas pattern.

2.  Moderate fecal loading in the ascending colon.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman hx RNY bypass with right-sided abdominal pain 
// r/o gallstones

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Liver or gallbladder ultrasound ___

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. The contour of the
liver is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. Main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 3 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 9.0 cm.

KIDNEYS: The right kidney measures 11.6 cm. The left kidney measures 11.9 cm.
Normal cortical echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation is seen
bilaterally. There is no evidence of masses, stones or hydronephrosis in the
kidneys.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

No cholelithiasis or cholecystitis. No focal liver lesions.
